briefing.opening: Good morning, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for July 28, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Climate Phenomena and Threats Sweeping Across the Globe
sections.content: Recently, extreme climate phenomena due to climate change have been intensifying worldwide. Domestically, a heatwave with daytime highs approaching 38 degrees Celsius has persisted, resulting in 302 heat-related illnesses over five days. As even Daegwallyeong was affected by the heatwave, the government raised the disaster alert level to its highest [5, 26, 27]. Across Europe and North America, large-scale wildfires, dubbed 'megafires' due to climate change, are sweeping through. Notably, European wildfires have surged by 57% in four years, with France and Spain, among others, dedicating all efforts to suppression [2, 31, 51, 69, 70]. As heatwaves and wildfires are increasingly perceived as 'unprecedented but not surprising' phenomena [59], an awareness is spreading that climate change is an emergency with radical impacts, exemplified by Prince William warning of its dangers [36, 55, 65].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Efforts for Climate Change Adaptation and Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Domestically, diverse efforts to address climate change are actively underway. Anseong City and Daegu Urban Development Corporation have initiated the development of climate change-resilient crop varieties and trial planting of southern tree species [1, 3]. Hamyang County is strengthening its climate change adaptation efforts, such as preventing heatwave damage to floricultural crops with temperature reduction technology and cooling scorching heat and tropical nights through urban forest creation [6, 29]. DGIST has secured core photocatalyst technology to convert greenhouse gases into future fuels [8], and Kyungpook National University has proposed directions for eco-friendly next-generation MOF technology, expected to utilize carbon-neutral materials [12]. Furthermore, carbon neutrality activities by various entities continue, including NongHyup Bank's carbon credit purchases [14], Yesan County's education to promote carbon neutrality practices [11], Namseoul University's training of carbon neutrality experts [13], and Jinju elementary students' milk carton recycling campaign [15]. The CEO of aT is also promoting the establishment of a dedicated climate change department alongside agricultural structural reform [7], demonstrating Korea's proactive commitment to addressing the climate crisis.

sections.title: ⚠️ Challenges and Policy Tasks in Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy for achieving carbon neutrality goals still faces numerous challenges. Eight out of ten domestic companies do not measure their greenhouse gas emissions [9, 16], and even local governments' evaluations of carbon neutrality implementation have been found to be inadequate, raising questions about the transparency of policy execution [10]. Amidst the shortage of power grids being identified as the biggest obstacle to renewable energy deployment [19], analysis shows that achieving the 2030 target of 100GW renewable energy is impossible under current trends, requiring a 3.6-fold acceleration of solar power generation [22, 23]. Renewable energy subsidies have increased 77-fold over the past 12 years, escalating financial burdens [17, 28], and market uncertainties are growing, with renewable energy stock prices falling due to stabilizing oil prices [25].

sections.title: 🌍 International Climate Action and Scientific Discourse
sections.content: The international community continues various discussions and actions to address climate change. TotalEnergies plans to appeal a French court's order for climate change business adaptation [32, 58], and in some regions, a rollback of climate policies is observed, such as the Ontario provincial government dismantling its climate change department [62]. Conversely, climate change funding has been announced for the Kentville and Annapolis Valley communities [56, 67], and international cooperation and investment continue, exemplified by the Global Carbon Council and Bhutan's Ministry of Environment and Climate Change signing an MoU [60]. In the scientific community, complex research findings are being presented, including simulation results indicating that low-level cloud loss amplifies global warming [43, 66], tropical species approaching their thermal limits [48], and discussions on the expansion of Antarctic ice area and the exaggeration of climate change [54]. Additionally, criticisms have been raised regarding the use of taxpayer funds for climate change research [41, 44, 46, 47, 50, 52, 53].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the globally spreading extreme weather phenomena, domestic and international efforts to address them, and the complex challenges in the transition to renewable energy. This is a time when continuous attention and action to overcome the climate crisis are becoming even more crucial. This concludes today's climate briefing.
